questions.q: What is the defining feature of a standard credit memo?
options: It is created against a specific original invoice and reduces that invoice's balance directly
It is never applied to any invoice
It can only be issued for credit card payments
It automatically increases the customer's credit limit
questions.explain: A standard credit memo's natural application is to a specific invoice, immediately reducing that invoice's open balance when applied.

questions.q: What is an on-account credit memo?
options: A credit tied to a specific invoice at the moment it's created
A credit balance on the customer's account that isn't tied to any specific invoice until someone applies it
A type of chargeback
A receipt that bounced
questions.explain: On-account credit memos sit as an available credit balance, reducing credit exposure immediately but not closing any particular invoice until applied.

questions.q: In the Harborline Retail Group example, what happened to the $12,500 invoice after the $500 standard credit memo was applied?
options: The invoice balance became $13,000
The invoice was merged with another invoice
The invoice balance dropped to $12,000
Nothing changed until the next billing cycle
questions.explain: A standard credit memo applied against a specific invoice reduces that invoice's open balance by the credit amount right away.

questions.q: Which scenario best fits issuing an on-account credit memo rather than a standard one?
options: Correcting an overbilled quantity on an invoice that's still open
A partial return of goods against the original invoice
An agreed quality allowance tied to one specific invoice
A goodwill credit issued before any future invoice is even known
questions.explain: A goodwill credit with no invoice yet to apply it against is a classic on-account scenario, since there's nothing specific to tie it to at creation time.

questions.q: What ultimately drives whether a credit memo transaction type expects to match a specific invoice?
options: The natural application setting on the credit memo transaction type
The customer's credit limit
The transaction source's numbering sequence
The ledger's functional currency
questions.explain: As covered in lesson 12, the transaction type's natural application attribute determines whether a credit memo expects to apply to an invoice or remain on-account.
